LESSON: TIME

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.6: Time
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, part of Measurement in Grade 4 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can we estimate time?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers in reading and telling time in a.m. and p.m. using digital and analogue clocks,

2. estimate time of the day using the shadow of a building or a tree that is in a convenient location,

3. change hours to minutes and minutes to hours,

4. change hours to days and days to hours,

5. convert days to weeks and weeks to days,

6. measure and record duration of events in hours and minutes using digital and analogue clocks,

7. work out addition involving units of time,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers in reading and telling time in a.m. and p.m. using digital and analogue clocks,
2. estimate time of the day using the shadow of a building or a tree that is in a convenient location,
3. change hours to minutes and minutes to hours,
4. change hours to days and days to hours,
5. convert days to weeks and weeks to days,
6. measure and record duration of events in hours and minutes using digital and analogue clocks,
7. work out addition involving units of time,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Imagination and creativity: learner explores new ways of estimating time using shadows of objects within

the environment.

• Digital literacy: learner discusses with others and records time using digital devices.

Values:
Integrity: learner consistently measures and records accurately the duration of events in hours and minutes

using digital or analogue clocks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: learner adheres to simple safety rules when telling and recording time using electronic

clock.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate estimation of time of the day to weather and climate in Social Studies.
